hypotheses.justification: hp can be deleted. If p is not prime, then `Nat.factorization m p = 0` and `Nat.factorization n p = 0`, because the factorization is supported on primes (`Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime`). That covers p = 0 and p = 1 as well. Then `ordCompl[p] m = m / p^0 = m` and `ordCompl[p] n = n`. The right side becomes `gcd m n * p ^ min 0 0 = gcd m n * 1 = gcd m n`, so the statement holds trivially. The proof splits with `by_cases hp : p.Prime`. The prime case is the existing proof. The non-prime case is `simp [Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime _ hp]`. The hypotheses hm and hn must stay. For m = 0 and p ∣ n with p prime, the left side is n, while the right side is `n / p^v * 1`, which differs when v > 0. Symmetrically, hn must stay.
